title: Multi-GPU parallelism performance study (NCCl & interconnect) WIP
content:
Purpose:
This working doc captures experiments and profiling notes for multi-GPU parallelism modes in the serving runtime. Focus areas: tensor parallel (TP) and pipeline parallel (PP) scaling behavior, NCCL-related collective overheads, and interconnect limits (NVLink vs. PCIe vs. InfiniBand). The goal is to identify dominant bottlenecks for production inference workloads and propose mitigations we can implement in the runtime.

High-level summary / takeaways so far (WIP):
- For small- to medium-sized models (<=13B) TP alone rarely helps on nodes with fast NVLink: single-node TP gives modest throughput gains but often hurts latency at small batch sizes because of increased cross-GPU synchronizations.
- For large models (70B+), PP remains necessary; however, stage imbalance and micro-batching overheads cause significant latency variance.
- NCCL all-reduce and peer-to-peer latencies dominate when we do frequent KV-cache exchanges or optimizer-like collectives for server-side sharding (we simulate weight-sharded inference). NCCL bandwidth saturates NVLink ~50-80 GB/s depending on topology and message sizes.
- Interconnect topology matters more than raw GPU count. A 4xA100 node with full NVLink mesh outperforms a 8x A100 node connected only by PCIe in many realistic workloads.

Hardware and software baseline used in experiments:
- Nodes: DGX A100 (8x A100 40GB) with full NVLink mesh (NVLink-3), Mellanox HDR100 InfiniBand for multi-node tests. Also tested on cloud instances: g5n.12x and p4d-like instances.
- Models: 7B (decoder-only), 13B, 34B, 70B (sharded across devices). Quantization: FP16 and 8-bit (GPTQ-like) for some runs.
- Frameworks: PyTorch 2.2 + torch.distributed, DeepSpeed inference and Megatron-LM sharded inference harnesses. NCCL 2.16+, CUDA 11.8/12.1 depending on node.
- Workloads: single request end-to-end latency (batch=1), stable streaming (tokens/sec per GPU), and synthetic microbenchmarks (all-reduce latency with varying message sizes, p2p latency).

Methodology / instrumentation:
- We instrumented: GPU utilization (nvidia-smi/pynvml), per-GPU device-to-device bandwidth (nvprof/ncu and custom NCCL trace logs), NCCL traces (NCCL env logging + NCCL_DEBUG=INFO for microbenchmarks), OS metrics (ethtool, ifconfig for link speed), and runtime traces (distributed profiler hooks in serving runtime to measure per-stage durations: forward, kv-exchange, collectives, GPU memcpy).
- Profiling pattern: run 5 cold requests to prime KV cache then run 50 steady-state requests. Capture per-token latency and GPU-side operation breakdown (percent of time in kernel vs memcopy vs sync).

Key experiment results (representative):
1) Single-node TP scaling (4 GPUs, local NVLink full mesh) for 13B model, batch=1 streaming (tokens/s):
- baseline (no TP, model replicated on 1 GPU): 12 tokens/s, p50 latency 420ms
- TP (4-way model parallel, same total batch): 28 tokens/s, p50 latency 480ms
Observations: throughput increases ~2.3x but latency increases ~15% due to additional cross-GPU syncs per token. For higher batch sizes (batch=8) TP shows more favorable latency/throughput tradeoff.

2) Pipeline parallel + micro-batching (70B across 8 GPUs):
- naive PP with micro-batch size 1: throughput 4 tokens/s, p50 latency 1.9s, high tail
- PP + micro-batch 8: throughput 22 tokens/s, p50 latency 650ms
Observations: micro-batching critical for utilization but introduces head-of-line latency for single-token requests. Our routing policy should avoid PP micro-batched nodes for low-latency tiers.

3) NCCL / collective overhead profiling (all-reduce microbenchmark on DGX A100):
- Message sizes < 64KB: latency dominated by NCCL kick overhead (~10-20us) — inefficient to do frequent small collectives.
- Message sizes 256KB-8MB: NVLink bandwidth approaching 60-75GB/s depending on pair and ring placement; cross-node IB gives ~8-12GB/s for small messages but scales better at >1MB messages.

4) Multi-node scaling (2 nodes x 8 GPUs, 16 GPUs total) for 70B PP:
- Throughput scaling ~1.7x going from 8->16 GPUs (expected ideal 2x) because inter-node stage edges cause pipeline stall and added latency from InfiniBand collectives.
- Host NIC and RDMA config mattered: enabling hugepages, setting mlx5 core driver tuning and disabling adaptive rx/tx improved p2p throughput ~15%.

Profiling traces / common hotspots found:
- Frequent small NCCL collectives during KV-cache synchronization. In our serving pattern, each token generation step ends up triggering small-ish p2p copies to assemble KV shards — this is the single biggest source of overhead at small batch sizes.
- Stage imbalance in PP: some layers are heavier (attention + MLP) and not evenly divisible causing one stage to be a straggler every micro-batch.
- PCIe host-to-device copies when model weights are sharded across host memory for large models (bad config). We saw memcpy D->H / H->D spikes when page faults occurred (missed pinning).
- NCCL topology sensitivity: ring vs tree algorithms showed different perf depending on message size and mesh connectivity. Default NCCL heuristics sometimes pick suboptimal algorithms for our small-message per-token workloads.

Tuning knobs we tried and preliminary effects:
- Fuse small NCCL collectives: batching KV exchanges across N steps reduced collective count by 4x and reduced per-token latency by ~28% at batch=1, at the cost of increased memory usage and slightly stale KV readouts.
- NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=NVL (force NVLink p2p) and NCCL_ALGO=RING/TREE manual overrides improved performance in specific topologies; needs topology-aware selection in runtime.
- Pinning host buffers (cudaHostAlloc) and using cudaMemcpyAsync with streams reduced host-GPU memcpy spikes.
- Increasing micro-batch size or enabling dynamic batching on the frontend is the simplest latency/throughput lever, but not acceptable for strict low-latency SLAs.
- Operator fusion and kernel autotuning (cuBLAS/cutlass config) improved per-GPU kernel time by 10-15% for MLP-heavy layers.

Recommended runtime-level mitigations (actionable):
1) Topology-aware collective planner: query NVLINK/PCIe topology and select NCCL algorithm/peer-ordering per model and message-size profile. Implement a small decision table at model load time.
2) KV-exchange fusion: add an option to fuse per-token KV transfers across K steps with a bounded staleness parameter. Expose as a per-route config (low-latency routes keep staleness=0).
3) Adaptive parallelism selection: for given model and node topology, pick replication vs TP vs PP based on expected p50/p99 SLO. E.g., avoid TP for batch=1 13B on NVLink and prefer replication with optimized kernel paths.
4) Micro-batching policy: prefer dynamic batcher that aggregates requests up to latency budget and avoid sending into PP nodes if route latency budget is tight. This requires runtime routing integration (console + routing policies).
5) NCCL env tuning and pinning: set recommended NCCL envs in our docker images and pin host buffers in our mem alloc layer.

Open questions / experiments to run next:
- More exhaustive topology space: compare 4x NVLink partial meshes and 8x PCIe-only with the same total GPU memory. We need to quantify the NVLink premium (cost vs perf) for typical inference workloads.
- Measure the effect of newer NCCL versions and CUDA 12.x on small-message latency (NCCL releases claim improvements for small collectives).
- Test alternative collective frameworks (e.g., custom RDMA-based p2p for KV exchange) to avoid NCCL scheduling overhead for tiny messages.
- Investigate scheduler-level pre-warming of KV cache to hide exchange latency for known repeated prompt patterns.
- Evaluate whether model-architectural optimizations (moving KV store to pinned host memory with RDMA) yield net improvements vs added complexity.

Notes / runbook snippets (commands we used):
- NCCL microbenchmark: 
  NCCL_DEBUG=INFO ./nccl-tests/build/all_reduce_perf -b 8 -e 8M -f 2 -g 8
- Torch distributed launch for 8 GPUs single node: 
  python -m torch.distributed.run --nproc_per_node=8 examples/inference_serving.py --model my-13b --parallel tensor --tp-size 4
- DeepSpeed inference launch (sharded): 
  deepspeed --num_gpus 8 ds_infer.py --model 70b --micro_batch_size 1 --pipeline_parallel_degree 8

Appendix: quick checklist for reproducibility when running these experiments:
- Confirm NVLink topology: lspci + nvidia-smi topo -m, record output.
- Set NCCL_DEBUG=INFO and capture logs.
- Ensure infiniband MTU and mlx5 settings (ethtool -S, sysctl net.core.rmem_max).
- Use pinned host buffers in benchmark harness and verify via nvprof that no host page faults occurred.

Concluding remark:
We have identified small-message NCCL collectives and PP stage imbalance as the two highest-priority engineering targets for improving multi-GPU inference latency and scaling. Next steps: (A) implement topology-aware NCCL selection and KV-exchange fusion prototype (Rahul / Miguel), (B) run full sweep comparing NVLink vs PCIe topologies with quantized models (Emily), (C) prototype alternative tiny-message p2p (Victor).
